_why: The #1929 doc-SQL gate parses THREE files. Its own debt register records that 1805 of 1988 ```sql fences under docs/ across 191 files are inventory-only — counted, never parsed. That gap has concrete cost: #1956 stage A could migrate only 45 of 131 downstream-form doc sites, because the other 86 live in files nothing can verify, and hand-editing unverifiable SQL is what produced five wrong corpus counts on that issue. Ungated doc SQL also rots silently: SQL_GRAMMAR_RULES.md's 'Correct Order' example had NEVER parsed, COPY_PASTE_EXAMPLES.md carried a WITH (config_file = ...) shape the engine rejects, and its UNION ALL example split wrongly — each found only because that file happened to be inside the enforced three.

anchors._note: the three-file enforced list to widen. The module doc explains WHY it is a fixed list rather than a directory walk — read that before changing its shape.

the debt register: 191 files, 1805 blocks, computed 2026-08-29. It fails in BOTH directions — a new ungated block is a regression, a stale entry must be deleted. Every file promoted to ENFORCED_FILES must leave this list.

the allowlist for genuine engine gaps, keyed (file, anchor, reason, issue). Promoting files WILL surface real breakage; an entry here needs a filed issue, and is NOT a way to silence a doc that is simply wrong.

blast_radius._note: Small in code, large in data: the decision surface is 191 .md files carrying 1805 fences. The work is mostly CLASSIFICATION (executable SQL vs prose that quotes SQL), and the bulk action is retagging non-executable fences ```sql -> ```text, which is cheap and safe. Only the executable residue earns a place on ENFORCED_FILES, and each promotion surfaces real breakage.

grammar_reference._note: Canonical clause order after #1962: SELECT -> FROM -> JOIN -> WHERE -> WINDOW -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT. A Kafka sink needs all three of '<name>.type', '<name>.bootstrap.servers', '<name>.topic'. Known unimplemented shapes that will surface: `FROM x AS y` (#1959) and `EMIT FINAL ORDER BY` (#1960) — both are ENGINE gaps, so allowlist with the issue number rather than rewriting the doc.

tests._note: The register must keep failing in BOTH directions after the change: a newly added ungated block is a regression, and an entry for a file that is now enforced or retagged is stale and must be deleted. A promotion that leaves its old register entry in place is the failure mode to guard.

stop_conditions: promoting a file surfaces more than 10 new parse failures — STOP and report the list rather than mass-allowlisting; that many failures means the file needs classification work first
you cannot tell whether a fence is executable SQL or illustrative prose — STOP and report those files; guessing is what this issue exists to stop
closing a failure requires editing SQL whose meaning you cannot verify — STOP; that is the exact hazard #1956 hit
